tasks.short: Drill, attach lifting equipment and direct stone removal

steps.what: Read the current stone identification and approved lifting instructions
Assess the stone and drill the required holes
Insert dogs or attach slings and inspect the attachment
Direct removal through live signals and observation

tasks.design: Keep drilling, attachment and live direction with the trained rock splitter. A current lifting-instruction view in {DOCS} can support the separately counted reading step, but the instructions still require full reading and application to this stone; neither a template nor a records app changes that work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on physical access, stone condition and live coordination rather than transcription.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document access can provide the current instruction, with no assumed new labour saving.
tasks.still_hard: Stone condition and changing lifting conditions require immediate human observation and coordination.
tasks.human_edge: The worker connects physical condition, attachment and live signals while retaining responsibility for stopping work.
tasks.altitude: The worker's week and decision rights stay the same.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: drilling, attachment inspection and live removal direction remain physical quarry work; document access does not perform them.

assumptions: Boundary is this splitter's stone preparation and live direction, including separately counted instruction reading. Shares are provisional task scenarios, not measured times.

The site planning process produces the stone identifier and current lifting instruction before s1. The splitter matches these to the physical stone; absent or inconsistent instructions require human clarification, not generated substitutes.

Record, report and send boundaries were considered separately: this task statement does not assign a removal tally, billing ticket or lifting-plan authorship to the splitter. Live signals in s4 are the direction itself, not an uncounted document or electronic send. If an actual splitter-owned tally or report accompanies removal, add and assess that write with the native quarry record form before using this zero-saving estimate.

Native current-document access is assessed before custom code. Reading still needs the whole applicable instruction; no repeated manual lookup or re-key baseline has been established. Equipment operation and machine runtime earn no labour saving.
No implementation is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this worker also owns a stone-removal tally or exception report
Whether the existing instruction view already displays the correct revision at the workface
research_questions: Observe a removal and isolate any actual tally, lookup, report or send performed by the splitter; can a native form change its manual work?

incremental.description: No new automation or recurring upkeep proposed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All 100 focal points remain: instruction reading 5, drilling 40, attachment 30 and live direction 25. A paper-only instruction case also retains all work; no recurring implementation upkeep is added. Additional observed record work requires a revised graph rather than an assumed saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Physical stone preparation and live direction remain the role's work.
skills_to_grow: Recognise instruction revisions and report discrepancies through existing site arrangements
role.ambitious_version: No new service is justified by this task's digital opportunity.
